3. Changed files (commit 37862e2953e3de7d413a2dc290b8e31e179a032e)
- plugins/pipeline-core/scripts/architecture-adoption.mjs: prepare --out. Boundary checked lexically BEFORE the request is built (a relative value resolves against --root; outside scratch/, the scratch dir itself, or another command refuses with a message naming scratch/ and exits 1, writing nothing); then the filesystem half (symlinked scratch/, real parent outside real scratch/, symlink/hardlink/non-regular existing target all refuse). One byte string feeds the file and stdout, so the file is byte-identical to the stdout form by construction. A one-line 'adoption request written: scratch/...' note goes to stderr.
- plugins/pipeline-core/scripts/po-human-approval.mjs: sign-intent --request accepts pipeline.adoption-approval-request.v1 via intent.sha256; new describeAdoptionApprovalRequest() discloses digest, decision, decision ref, every scope entry, rationale, dates, candidate and repository fingerprint from the request alone; a non-binding request throws 'the adoption approval request does not bind its exact subject and intent digest' before assertSigningReadyBeforePrompt, confirmation, key access or signing. Proof shape and scratch mirror unchanged (scratchSiblingPath already maps adoption-request-1.json to adoption-proof-1.json).

Design choice (describer): it does NOT call verifyAdoptionAuthority() (that rebinds repository fingerprint, candidate and live snapshot; the pin's signing root has none of them, and a PO may sign a request for another root) and no forbidden lib file was touched. It requires: exact top-level keys; intent.sha256 equal to the sign-intent digest and to sha256(canonical(intent.value)); sha256(canonical(subject)) equal to subjectSha256 and to intent.value.subjectSha256; intent.value.kind 'architecture-adoption', policyRevision 'adoption-authority-v1', decision and candidate agreeing with the subject; strict shapes for every disclosed field. Free text (decision ref, rationale, each scope entry) is rendered through JSON.stringify so a hostile request cannot inject a disclosure line. The plan/spec digest derivation is NOT repeated here: verifyAdoptionAuthority() re-derives the full intent at apply time, so this is disclosure, never authority.
